page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the c3 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the x86_64 architecture and includes advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1618.89 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1713.0. However, multi-core and memory subsystem benchmarks generally fall into the weak or poor categories. The stress-ng multi-core score is 3315.66, and the Geekbench multi-core score is 3813.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 28.42 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 21.13 GB/sec for large block write operations. Static web serving throughput is measured at 6.68 GB/sec, which represents average performance.

The instance exhibits a clear tradeoff between single-threaded execution and multi-threaded or memory-intensive operations. While single-threaded gzip compression (26.37 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (11.4 GB/sec) perform at average levels, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression drops to a poor rating at 21.71 GB/sec. Similarly, database operations and Redis SET operations are rated as weak. This hardware profile is suited for general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, and lightweight single-threaded applications rather than memory-bound databases or highly parallelized compute tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor at 2.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it includes advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast: single-core capabilities are average, as demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1713.0, whereas multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are consistently weak. For example, the stress-ng multi-core score is 3315.66, and large-block memory read bandwidth is limited to 28.42 GB/sec. Consequently, this instance is best suited for basic web serving, text processing, and light single-threaded applications, while representing a performance tradeoff for database operations and highly parallelized workloads.
